Shizuku Tools
Performance Game Mode
Ask Android to run the game in Performance Game Mode (Android 12+). Applies to Dynamic and Performance. The effect depends on the ROM and on the game.
Clean memory
Close cached background apps. The game in front is never touched.
Background limiter
While you play, stop other installed apps that are running from working in the background. Original settings are restored when the game ends. Messages from limited apps can arrive late.
Always allowed
Launcher, keyboard, SMS and dialer apps are always kept. Add any other app you do not want limited.
Add app
Choose the apps the limiter must never touch in Explore mode, under Shizuku Tools.
Turn off Battery Saver
Battery Saver slows the CPU. It is turned off when a game starts and is not turned back on automatically.
Fixed performance mode (experimental)
Asks the vendor power service for sustained performance in Performance mode. Many ROMs ignore it. Turned off again when the game ends.
What the modes do without root

Balance: leaves system Game Mode untouched. Dynamic: Performance Game Mode, drops to Standard when the phone reports moderate thermal throttling, returns when it cools. Performance: Performance Game Mode, plus fixed performance mode if you enabled it.
Needs root (not possible here)

CPU and GPU frequency limits, governor, process priority, scheduler boost, storage read-ahead and swap pressure write to kernel files that the Shizuku ADB shell cannot change. They are not faked. If Shizuku itself runs as root they work too.
Only changes that Android really accepts are applied, and every one is restored when the session ends, even if ZKM was closed in the middle of a game.

Working modes

Root: every feature. Shizuku running as root: same as Root. Shizuku ADB: Game Mode, memory clean, background limiter, refresh rate, screenshot and recording, Battery Saver off. Basic: nothing privileged. Items that your mode cannot do are shown disabled, never faked.
CPU modes: Balance, Dynamic, Performance

With root they set the governor and frequency limits of each CPU cluster. Without root they map to Android Game Mode: Balance leaves it alone, Dynamic and Performance request Performance Game Mode, and Dynamic backs off when the phone gets hot.
Custom Mode and Tools

Custom Mode edits CPU and GPU limits per mode and needs root to write them. Root Tools (root) and Shizuku Tools (no root) hold the system boosts that run when a game starts and are restored when it ends. The thermal guard works in both.
Handheld or Explore

Handheld is the landscape console with the Mecha look. Explore is one scrolling screen that follows your Wallpaper Style. Both share the same settings, so switching never loses anything. Use the switch at the top to change.
Game Space
Launches your games with a tuned loadout and gives an in-game panel with live stats, quick toggles and performance modes. It works in Root mode and in Shizuku (no root) mode.
Master switch: turns detection on. Add games with Add game; each game can keep its own profile or follow the global defaults.
Permissions: Usage Access finds the game in front, Display over other apps shows the panel. Both are requested only here.
Per session ZKM can set Do Not Disturb, block heads-up notifications, lock brightness mode and refresh rate, and request Game Mode. Every value is saved first and put back when you leave the game.

Modes: Balance, Dynamic and Performance. With root they control CPU governor and frequency per cluster. In Shizuku ADB mode they map to Android Game Mode, and Dynamic steps down when the phone reports thermal throttling.

Shizuku Tools (no root): Performance Game Mode, memory clean, background limiter with an always-allowed list, Battery Saver off, and an experimental fixed performance mode. Root Tools adds process priority, scheduler boost, read-ahead and swap pressure.
Panel styles: Energy Cube (landscape hub with left and right menus) or Compact. Handheld is the Mecha console; Explore is the scrolling screen. Both use the same settings.
The Energy Cube splash only lists what really happened in this session. If your mode cannot do something, it is simply not listed.

Game Mode and fixed performance depend on the ROM and on each game; some ignore them. CPU and GPU frequency control needs root. The background limiter can delay messages from limited apps while you play.
Game Space with Shizuku (no root)

Start Shizuku (wireless debugging or adb), grant ZKM access, then choose ADB mode in Settings. Game Space then uses only commands the shell user may run: Game Mode, memory clean, appops, settings and power commands. Kernel files such as CPU governor or GPU clocks cannot be written from that shell, so those controls stay disabled instead of pretending. If your Shizuku runs as root, ZKM detects it and unlocks the root features automatically.
Why is there no CPU frequency slider in Shizuku mode?

Android only lets root change CPU and GPU frequency. A no-root app that shows such a slider would be doing nothing. ZKM instead uses what Android officially allows: Game Mode, thermal-aware stepping and background limiting. Custom Mode values are still saved and used the moment you switch to Root.
